Periodic function
A
periodic function
is a
function
that repeats its values at regular intervals. For example, the trigonometric functions, which are used to describe
waves
and other repeating phenomena, are periodic. Many aspects of the natural world have periodic behavior, such as the
phases of the Moon
, the swinging of a
pendulum
, and the
beating
of a heart.
The length of the interval over which a periodic function repeats is called its
period
. Any function that is not periodic is called
aperiodic
.

natural numbers
